paragraphs: Long-context models face a memory trade-off: compressing earlier information saves resources but can lose detail, while retaining a growing attention cache becomes expensive. This paper combines these approaches through separate short-term and long-term memories. Recent information stays in a sliding window of the Transformer’s attention cache, while an Artificial Hippocampus Network recurrently compresses information that leaves the window.

The researchers implement the compression module using Mamba2, DeltaNet, and GatedDeltaNet. They train it through self-distillation while freezing every parameter of the original language model. At inference, the default attention window holds 32k tokens, and the additional memory module activates only when the sequence exceeds that length.

On LV-Eval and InfiniteBench, the augmented models consistently beat sliding-window baselines and perform comparably to, or better than, full attention with substantially lower resource requirements. For Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct at 128k tokens, the reported example reduces inference FLOPs by 40.5% and cache memory by 74.0%, while raising the average LV-Eval score from 4.41 to 5.88. These results support learned compression as a useful complement to detailed recent memory.
icml-2026-artificial-hippocampus-network.tldr: Artificial Hippocampus Networks compress older context into fixed-size memory while retaining recent attention, improving long-context efficiency and benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Neural solvers can learn to make decisions for packing and routing problems, but their performance often becomes brittle when the problem distribution changes. This paper examines a distinction within that decision process: identifying several promising actions versus choosing the single best action. The authors theoretically and experimentally support what they call the Satisficing Generalization Edge: the former task generalizes more readily.

Adaptive Selection After Proposal, or ASAP, builds this distinction into the solver. A proposal policy filters the available actions into promising candidates, and a separate selection policy decides among them. This separation provides a focused target for adaptation: the selection policy can be rapidly fine-tuned when the solver encounters a new distribution. A two-phase training procedure uses Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning to prepare the model for that adjustment.

Experiments cover three-dimensional bin packing, the traveling salesman problem, and capacitated vehicle routing. ASAP improves the generalization of state-of-the-art baselines and delivers better online adaptation on out-of-distribution instances. The findings support separating candidate generation from final choice as a practical way to make learned optimization more adaptable.
icml-2026-asap-exploiting-the-satisficin.tldr: ASAP separates proposing promising actions from selecting one, enabling neural optimization solvers to adapt more effectively to new distributions.

paragraphs: Biological foundation models often reuse general-purpose architectures even though genomic and proteomic sequences have distinct structural and functional patterns. BioArc investigates whether architecture discovery can better match these patterns. Its central idea is to let data guide the composition of a model instead of relying primarily on designers’ intuition about which architecture should work.

The framework uses neural architecture search over a heterogeneous collection of building blocks, allowing hybrid architectures rather than restricting the search to a single uniform design family. It also studies architecture together with tokenization and training across biological modalities. This matters because the way biological inputs are represented and the way a network processes them are treated as interacting design choices.

The discovered architectures surpass state-of-the-art models while being up to 25 times smaller. The authors derive empirical design principles and report evidence that their architectures capture biological patterns hierarchically. They also introduce an agentic framework for predicting suitable architectures for new tasks. Together, these contributions position automated architecture discovery as a route to more efficient biological foundation models and specialized networks.
icml-2026-bioarc-discovering-optimal-neu.tldr: BioArc searches heterogeneous neural architectures to discover biological models that outperform existing designs while being up to 25 times smaller.

paragraphs: Some mathematical accounts of deep Transformers predict that token representations eventually collapse into a single cluster. This paper revisits that prediction by including randomness from the initialization of value matrices. The authors argue that deterministic weight assumptions miss a source of stochastic behavior present in standard Transformer initialization.

Their analysis considers token-wise RMS normalization and a particular diffusion scaling as the number of layers tends to infinity. Under those conditions, discrete token updates converge to an interacting-particle system on a sphere. All tokens experience a shared matrix-valued Brownian noise. Within this limiting system, initialization noise prevents the single-cluster collapse predicted by deterministic models.

For two tokens, the authors prove a phase transition controlled by interaction strength and representation dimension. Configurations with tokens at opposite points on the sphere can become attracting with positive probability. Numerical experiments confirm the transition, show that such opposite-point formations also persist with more tokens, and find that suppressing the intrinsic noise reduces accuracy. The result makes initialization randomness part of the explanation of token organization, rather than an incidental detail.
icml-2026-clustering-in-deep-stochastic-.tldr: Under an infinite-depth stochastic model, random initialization prevents token collapse and can make opposite-point token configurations attracting.

paragraphs: COFT addresses societal bias expressed during a language model’s generated reasoning by changing token selection at inference time. It works with a frozen causal language model, so the intervention does not require retraining. The method aims to reduce the influence of sensitive attributes while retaining useful reasoning and fluent language.

First, COFT constructs a second prompt in which sensitive spans are replaced with neutral tokens. It then combines information from the original and masked prompts’ token-score distributions to attenuate attribute-driven bias. Finally, dual-branch split-conformal calibration produces candidate token sets at a user-selected risk level. Its distribution-free marginal validity guarantee depends on exchangeability and applies to these per-step sets.

Across six models and multiple bias benchmarks, COFT reduces standard bias measures by 30–55%, with a median reduction of 38%. Reasoning accuracy stays within run-to-run noise margins, while task utility and language quality are preserved. Reported computational overhead is at most 11%, equivalent to one additional cached forward pass. The contribution combines an explicit decoding intervention with calibrated token sets and measured bias reductions.
icml-2026-coft-counterfactualconformal-d.tldr: COFT combines masked-prompt comparisons and conformal calibration to reduce measured reasoning biases without retraining, with validity guarantees under exchangeability.

paragraphs: An agent can plan by combining existing policies as actions that unfold over time, rather than deciding every primitive movement separately. Such combinations can solve tasks that no individual policy can complete. The difficulty is predicting where a sequence of policies will take the agent, because errors can compound over long planning horizons.

This paper learns jumpy world models that predict the states visited under pretrained policies across several timescales. The models learn off-policy and build on Temporal Difference Flows. A new consistency objective aligns predictions made at different timescales, improving long-horizon predictive accuracy. The authors then combine these generative predictions to estimate the value of arbitrary policy sequences executed over varying durations.

On challenging manipulation and navigation tasks, the approach significantly improves zero-shot performance across a broad range of base policies. For long-horizon tasks, the reported average relative improvement over planning with primitive actions is 200%. These findings support learning temporally extended predictions as a way to make reusable policies more useful for planning, with cross-timescale consistency helping those predictions remain coherent.
icml-2026-compositional-planning-with-ju.tldr: Jumpy world models predict pretrained policies’ effects across timescales, improving zero-shot planning by composing those policies into longer behaviors.

paragraphs: Federated fine-tuning lets distributed clients collaborate on adapting a model, but large models impose substantial resource and communication costs. Low-Rank Adaptation reduces the number of trainable parameters. This paper finds that its restricted representation can also amplify sensitivity to noise, contributing to overfitting and biased aggregation of client updates.

The authors examine the two matrices inside a LoRA adapter and identify different behavior. The down-projection matrix A extracts relatively stable general features, while the up-projection matrix B is more susceptible to fitting noise. FedDR-LoRA uses this asymmetry to separate robust feature learning from noise modeling through two branches. Negative learning in the noisy branch helps reduce interference from noise.

The aggregation procedure also treats the matrices differently: it combines B across clients to establish global consensus while retaining local feature alignment in A. Across various noisy federated settings, the method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. Its contribution is to make robustness depend on the adapter’s internal structure, giving feature extraction, noise handling, and cross-client aggregation distinct roles.
icml-2026-decoupled-low-rank-adaptation-.tldr: FedDR-LoRA treats LoRA’s two matrices differently to separate noise modeling from robust learning and improve noisy federated fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Quantization makes models more efficient by representing their numerical values at lower precision, but it often reduces accuracy. Function-preserving transformations can lessen that damage, although why they help has lacked a principled explanation. This paper analyzes quantization in linear layers using the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio, a measure of useful signal relative to the error introduced.

For uniform integer quantization at a fixed bit width, the analysis separates this ratio into two factors. Concentration describes the spread and outliers of weights and activations. Alignment describes how their dominant directions of variation relate. The resulting insight is that improving alignment can reduce quantization error alongside approaches that focus on concentration.

The proposed Concentration–Alignment Transforms use a covariance estimate from a small calibration set to improve both factors jointly. This lightweight linear transformation approximately maximizes the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio. Across several language models at 4-bit precision, it consistently matches or exceeds earlier transformation-based methods. The findings connect a mathematical decomposition of quantization error to a concrete calibration procedure for reducing it.
icml-2026-dissecting-quantization-error-.tldr: CAT reduces quantization error by jointly improving the concentration and directional alignment of weights and activations.

paragraphs: Causal abstraction connects detailed and coarse descriptions of the same system while seeking agreement about the effects of interventions. Existing learning methods assume that the distributions of external influences are fixed and correctly specified. This paper addresses the resulting vulnerability when environments change or those distributional assumptions are inaccurate.

The authors introduce distributionally robust causal abstractions and algorithms for learning them. Their formulation uses constrained min-max optimization: it seeks an abstraction while accounting for unfavorable distributions within a specified set. These Wasserstein ambiguity sets describe the distributional alternatives considered during learning, making the range of uncertainty part of the optimization problem.

The paper provides theoretical guarantees for empirical and Gaussian environments, including guidance for choosing ambiguity-set radii and quantitative bounds on worst-case abstraction error. Experiments across different problems and abstraction-learning methods show robustness to environmental changes. They also provide evidence of robustness when causal structure or intervention mappings are misspecified. The contribution therefore extends causal abstraction learning from a single assumed environment toward explicitly accounting for uncertainty in the environments being related.
icml-2026-distributionally-robust-causal.tldr: This framework learns causal abstractions against distributional uncertainty, with worst-case error guarantees and empirical robustness to several forms of misspecification.

paragraphs: Sequence models often learn dynamics at the temporal or spatial scale seen during training, making much longer sequences or higher-resolution inputs difficult to handle. Dynamic Fractal Mamba addresses this by recursively applying one shared state-space operator across multiple scales. The same parameters govern each recursion depth, encouraging related behavior as the scale changes.

The model increases its effective time step exponentially across scales. This expands the receptive field exponentially while retaining linear computational complexity. A learned, content-aware coarse-graining module aggregates representations across scales, while reconstruction and cross-scale consistency objectives help stabilize recursive training. Together, these components combine broad coverage with explicit pressure for coherent representations at different resolutions.

Evaluations cover long-range time-series forecasting, spatial transcriptomics, and computational pathology. Across these tasks, the model outperforms Transformer and flat Mamba baselines while using fewer parameters. Models trained on short sequences or low-resolution inputs also generalize without additional training to substantially larger unseen scales. The findings support recursive parameter sharing as an effective architectural bias for efficient, scale-consistent representations in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-dynamic-fractal-mamba-a-neural.tldr: DF-Mamba shares a recursive state-space operator across scales, enabling efficient modeling and zero-shot generalization to larger temporal and spatial inputs.

paragraphs: This paper studies privacy accounting when a user’s data participates in k steps selected uniformly at random from t possible steps. This random-allocation scheme has shown utility advantages over standard Poisson sampling. Previous analyses, however, can produce loose privacy parameters and use divergence measures that introduce additional overhead when accounting for accumulated privacy loss.

The authors show that the privacy loss distribution for random allocation can be computed efficiently for any differentially private algorithm. Working with this distribution directly addresses the accounting problem underlying the earlier bounds. To support the computation, they develop a general concept called privacy loss distribution realization.

For the Gaussian mechanism, their results show that random allocation offers a privacy–utility trade-off at least as good as Poisson subsampling, and they identify it as better suited to DP-SGD training. The new accounting tools also extend accurate treatment to subsampling cases that previously required manual analysis tailored to the noise mechanism. The contribution combines a comparison of sampling schemes with a more general way to calculate their privacy costs.
icml-2026-efficient-privacy-loss-account.tldr: New privacy-loss accounting tools efficiently analyze random allocation and show a Gaussian-mechanism privacy–utility trade-off at least as good as Poisson subsampling.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction returns a set of possible labels with a specified probability of containing the correct one. Smaller sets are usually preferable, but size alone may miss what users need. When labels belong to meaningful groups, a set concentrated within fewer groups can be easier to interpret or connect to downstream actions.

This paper modifies the conformal scoring function by adding a penalty for errors that cross group boundaries. The authors prove benefits for group-related measures. They also show mathematically that, for common class partitions, the modification can reduce average prediction-set size for any conformal score function. That result connects semantic organization to the usual goal of producing compact sets.

The analysis identifies class similarity as the source of the improvement. It motivates another version that uses the model’s embeddings, avoiding the need for a human-defined semantic partition. An empirical study across prominent conformal methods, multiple models, and several datasets finds consistent improvements. The approach therefore offers both a way to make prediction sets more coherent and a broadly applicable route to reducing their size.
icml-2026-enhancing-conformal-prediction.tldr: Using class similarity in conformal scores can produce prediction sets that span fewer semantic groups and contain fewer labels.

paragraphs: A useful generative-model training loss measures differences between target and model log probabilities after subtracting their batch mean. This centering accommodates targets whose normalization is unknown. With samples from the current model, the established loss has gradients corresponding to KL divergence; with off-policy samples, it remains valid and retains the same global minimizer.

This paper extends that construction to the full family of f-divergences. It uses an established correspondence between translation-invariant losses and these divergences, adapting it to batch-wise policy optimization with unnormalized targets. The result is a family of low-variance surrogate objectives that can use off-policy data while inheriting properties of their associated divergences, including greater coverage of different modes.

The authors test these losses in molecular discovery with SynFlowNets, conditional sampling from diffusion models, and asynchronous language-model tuning. Across these applications, the models retain the predicted properties with both on-policy and off-policy data. The contribution gives training-objective design more flexibility: different distribution-matching preferences can be expressed without abandoning the useful batch-centered construction.
icml-2026-f-trajectory-balance-a-loss-fa.tldr: f-Trajectory Balance generalizes batch-centered training losses to f-divergences, supporting unnormalized targets and both on-policy and off-policy data.

paragraphs: Jailbreak research changes quickly, while evaluations can become outdated or difficult to compare because papers use different datasets, execution frameworks, and judging procedures. Jailbreak Foundry addresses this infrastructure problem by translating research papers into executable attack modules and evaluating them through a common framework. Its purpose is to make a continually updated benchmark more practical.

The system has three components. JBF-LIB supplies shared interfaces and reusable utilities, JBF-FORGE uses a multi-agent workflow to turn papers into modules, and JBF-EVAL standardizes evaluation. Shared infrastructure reduces how much implementation work must be repeated for each attack and makes it possible to evaluate the resulting modules together.

Across 30 reproduced attacks, the mean difference between reproduced and reported attack success rates is +0.26 percentage points. Attack-specific code is reduced by more than half relative to the original repositories, with an average reused-code ratio of 82.5%. The system also evaluates all 30 attacks on AdvBench across 10 target models using one consistent GPT-4o judge. These findings demonstrate practical reproduction and standardized comparison at the reported scale.
icml-2026-jailbreak-foundry-from-papers-.tldr: Jailbreak Foundry turns attack papers into reusable executable modules and standardizes their evaluation to support continually updated robustness benchmarks.

paragraphs: Bottleneck states connect otherwise distinct regions of an agent’s state space, making them useful landmarks for longer-duration behaviors. Existing methods often locate these states by analyzing the structure of a state-transition graph. That dependence makes them difficult to scale to high-dimensional or continuous environments, where an explicit graph is less convenient.

This paper introduces Value Power Strength, or VPS, which measures bottleneck properties through value functions. Its motivation comes from an analogy between the Bellman equation and Kirchhoff’s current law: the method examines how reward diffuses through a decision process. VPS can be estimated efficiently from value functions learned using random reward signals, and it applies to both discrete and continuous state spaces.

The authors use the resulting measurements to construct options that move agents toward or away from bottleneck regions. Experiments span tabular environments, continuous-control tasks, and Atari 2600 games. VPS identifies semantically meaningful bottlenecks, and the resulting options improve exploration. The approach connects interpretable temporal abstractions to value-function learning, offering an alternative to relying primarily on explicit transition-graph topology.
icml-2026-learning-interpretable-options.tldr: Value Power Strength identifies reward-diffusion bottlenecks from learned value functions and uses them to build interpretable options that improve exploration.

paragraphs: Time-series foundation models train on datasets whose temporal patterns can differ substantially. Olivia starts from the assumption that making these datasets more compatible in the spectral domain could improve pretraining and transfer. It uses normalized power spectral density, which characterizes how signal power is distributed across frequencies, as the basis for this harmonization.

Rather than directly solving an intractable minimization problem, the authors introduce Harmonizer, a module that reshapes spectral structure and implicitly harmonizes power spectral densities. Their theory connects this operation to a shared reparameterization of second-order temporal correlations. Further analysis shows that token interactions can be mediated efficiently through a compact collection of resonators, motivating HarmonicAttention in a low-dimensional interaction space.

Olivia combines these mechanisms into a time-series foundation model. Across TSLib, GIFT-Eval, and GluonTS benchmarks, it consistently achieves state-of-the-art forecasting results in zero-shot, few-shot, and full-shot settings. The results support the proposed combination of spectral harmonization and compact attention as a useful approach to learning from heterogeneous time-series datasets.
icml-2026-olivia-harmonizing-time-series.tldr: Olivia combines spectral harmonization with compact harmonic attention to improve forecasting across zero-shot, few-shot, and full-shot settings.

paragraphs: Reward models guide language-model alignment by scoring responses according to learned human preferences. When those scores contain systematic biases, a language model can learn undesirable behaviors that receive high rewards. This paper examines that problem by systematically measuring biases in five high-quality reward models, including state-of-the-art models.

The study finds persistent preferences related to response length, sycophancy, and overconfidence, despite previous work on these issues. It also identifies biases toward model-specific writing styles and answer order. The authors distinguish failures that can be addressed through linear intervention from those that resist it, making the complexity of a bias relevant to how it can be corrected.

They propose mechanistic reward shaping, a simple post-hoc intervention targeting low-complexity biases arising from spurious correlations. The method acts inside the reward model, uses little labeled data, and reduces the targeted biases without degrading reward quality. It also generalizes out of distribution and can be extended to new biases. The contribution pairs evidence that reward-model biases remain widespread with a targeted method for mitigating a tractable subset.
icml-2026-one-bias-after-another-mechani.tldr: The paper documents persistent reward-model biases and introduces a lightweight internal intervention that mitigates targeted low-complexity biases.

paragraphs: Self-consistency improves language-model reasoning by generating multiple responses and choosing the answer that appears most often. Its cost can become substantial when applied across many questions. This paper treats that procedure as a problem of estimating the most common answer, using mode estimation and voting theory to study how efficiently samples can be used.

The authors derive and empirically validate power-law scaling behavior across datasets. They also analyze approaches that assign a fixed number of samples to questions and approaches that adjust allocations dynamically. This connects the overall sampling budget to the decision of where additional generated responses should be spent during inference.

From that analysis, they introduce Blend-ASC, which dynamically allocates samples across questions. It uses 4.8 times fewer samples than vanilla self-consistency on average and outperforms both fixed- and dynamic-allocation baselines in sample efficiency. The method is hyperparameter-free and can accommodate any sample budget. Its contribution is to make the allocation of reasoning attempts an explicit part of the inference algorithm, improving the efficiency of repeated-answer voting.
icml-2026-optimal-self-consistency-for-e.tldr: Blend-ASC dynamically allocates reasoning samples across questions, using 4.8 times fewer samples than vanilla self-consistency on average.

paragraphs: Generated-video detectors are often evaluated on their ability to recognize outputs from unfamiliar generators. This paper identifies another factor that can make that apparent generalization misleading: the quality distribution of real videos. If real and synthetic training videos differ systematically in quality, a detector can learn that difference as a shortcut.

Testing on real videos with a similar quality profile can conceal the problem. The authors find that these detectors fail when the real videos instead have substantially different quality characteristics. Their response is to match the quality of real and fake training data, reducing the correlation between quality and the label the model is supposed to predict.

They then expand the training data to cover the quality spectrum more comprehensively. This encourages detection features that are less dependent on video quality and improves generalization across real videos with varying quality profiles. Extensive experiments show consistent improvements across diverse model backbones. The findings make the choice of real training and test data central to evaluating whether a detector has learned transferable evidence of synthetic generation.
icml-2026-real-data-lies-unveiling-and-c.tldr: Matching and broadening real and synthetic video quality reduces a misleading detection shortcut and improves generalization across real-video quality levels.

paragraphs: When a language-model agent turns a user’s intent into actions, the resulting outcome may prompt a counterfactual question: what would have happened if the intent had been expressed differently? This paper develops a framework for answering that question in autonomous control, combining causal modeling with formal reliability guarantees for the generated outcomes.

The framework represents the closed-loop interaction among the user, agent, and environment as a structural causal model. It uses probabilistic abduction to generate multiple candidate counterfactual outcomes, with test-time scaling supplying additional candidates. This gives the method a causal representation of the observed interaction from which to reason about an altered intent.

An offline calibration stage turns those candidates into conformal counterfactual generation sets. These sets are guaranteed to contain the true counterfactual outcome with high probability, so reliability is expressed through a collection of possible outcomes. In a wireless-network control application, the method shows significant advantages over naive re-execution baselines. The contribution links counterfactual analysis of user instructions to calibrated uncertainty in an agent’s possible effects.
icml-2026-should-i-have-expressed-a-diff.tldr: Conformal counterfactual generation produces calibrated sets of outcomes for differently expressed user intents in language-model-driven control.

paragraphs: This paper studies optimization problems in which one decision maker minimizes an objective while another maximizes it. The objective may be nonsmooth, with submodular structure on the minimizing side and concavity on the maximizing side. The authors consider both offline problems and online settings where the sequence of optimal decisions can change.

Their zeroth-order method combines two techniques suited to these different structures. For the minimizer, it uses a subgradient of the objective’s Lovász extension. For the maximizer, it applies Gaussian smoothing to estimate the gradient of a smoothed objective. This provides an algorithmic route for handling the two sides without requiring a smooth original objective.

In the offline setting, the authors prove convergence in expectation to an epsilon-saddle point. Online, they establish an expected duality-gap bound of order sqrt(N(1 + P̄_N)), where N counts iterations and P̄_N measures the movement of optimal decisions. The bound explicitly reflects how much that target sequence changes. The paper also supplies complexity analyses and hyperparameter choices, with numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results.
icml-2026-solving-the-offline-and-online.tldr: A zeroth-order method obtains expected offline convergence and an online duality-gap bound for nonsmooth submodular–concave optimization.

paragraphs: Audio jailbreak research often optimizes perturbations across an entire waveform to induce unsafe model responses. This paper asks whether such dense updates are necessary. By examining gradients aligned with audio tokens, the authors find that optimization signal is distributed unevenly: a small subset of token-associated audio regions carries much of the gradient energy.

Token-Aware Gradient Optimization, or TAGO, incorporates that observation into sparse optimization. At each iteration, it retains waveform gradients associated with high-energy audio tokens and masks the others. The method therefore concentrates updates on the regions identified as carrying the strongest optimization signal, directly testing how much of the dense update process is redundant.

Across three audio language models, TAGO outperforms the evaluated baselines while preserving strong attack success under substantial sparsification. In the Qwen3-Omni example, the reported ASR_l is 86% with one-quarter of tokens retained, compared with 87% under full retention. These findings show that dense waveform updates are largely redundant in the evaluated attacks and motivate attention to token-level gradient heterogeneity in both attack research and safety alignment.
icml-2026-sparse-tokens-suffice-jailbrea.tldr: TAGO shows that updating a small subset of high-gradient audio regions can preserve strong jailbreak success across evaluated audio language models.

paragraphs: Rectified Flow and Flow Matching have improved generative modeling, but their theoretical and design differences from existing diffusion models complicate the reuse of acceleration techniques. StreamFlow develops an acceleration pipeline specifically around flow-based generation. It combines changes to the formulation, algorithm design, and inference implementation.

The pipeline includes batch processing with a new velocity field and vectorized processing of batches containing heterogeneous time steps. It also uses dynamic TensorRT compilation to accelerate the new methods. These components address different parts of execution together: how generation updates are organized, how varied time steps are processed in batches, and how the resulting computations are compiled.

For 512-by-512 image generation, the abstract reports acceleration reaching 611%, compared with a typical 18% for existing public methods. This is presented as an experimental upper result, rather than a uniform speed gain for every setting. The paper’s contribution is an integrated route to faster flow-model generation, showing that coordinated changes across theory, batching, and implementation can deliver substantial acceleration in the reported experiments.
icml-2026-streamflow-theory-algorithm-an.tldr: StreamFlow combines flow-specific batching, vectorization, and dynamic compilation, reporting image-generation acceleration of up to 611%.

paragraphs: A model that accepts audio and video may still make decisions mainly from one input, even on tasks that call for combining them. This paper introduces Sensory PID to examine that behavior. Conditioned on language, it separates audio and video contributions into unique information, overlapping information, and information available through their combination.

Applied to omni-modal models, the analysis reveals a sensory synergy bottleneck: modality-specific information dominates decisions, with vision contributing more strongly. Shuffling modalities supports this asymmetry. Layer-by-layer analysis also finds a visual-first computation pattern, while changes to instructions indicate that language conditions sensory fusion in later processing stages.

The authors go beyond diagnosis by using PID signals to reweight samples. This provides initial evidence of improvements in multimodal reasoning and grounding, rather than establishing a general solution to the bottleneck. A separate vision–language analysis broadly confirms previously reported decision-level PID patterns across tasks, models, interventions, and layers. Together, the results offer a way to distinguish merely receiving multiple modalities from making decisions that use their joint information.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-modality.tldr: Sensory PID finds vision-dominated decisions and limited audio–video synergy, with initial evidence that its diagnostics can guide performance improvements.

paragraphs: For geometrically structured data, comparing features meaningfully can require accounting for their spatial alignment. The VBA-Transformer incorporates that alignment directly into attention. Its tokens pair a coordinate on a base manifold with a feature vector, using vector bundle theory to connect the geometric location and the information represented there.

Before computing similarity, a parallel transport mechanism aligns feature vectors across their local coordinate systems. Geometry therefore participates in the comparison operation itself, beyond being supplied as a positional encoding or external attention bias. The paper also analyzes invariance and stability under perturbations, alongside empirical tests of robust transport behavior.

On single-cell RNA sequencing benchmarks, VBA achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, with reported improvements over Transformer baselines exceeding 3–5%. It also delivers superior clustering on spatial transcriptomics and competitive accuracy on 3D point clouds. These results support the usefulness of intrinsic geometric alignment across the evaluated domains. The contribution combines a geometrically defined attention mechanism with theoretical analysis and empirical evidence spanning biological and three-dimensional data.
icml-2026-vba-vector-bundle-attention-fo.tldr: VBA aligns features across local coordinate systems before attention comparisons, improving biological benchmarks and achieving competitive 3D point-cloud accuracy.
